head: NRF2 transcriptional program
name: NRF2 transcriptional program (target genes, NRF2 expression, GSK3B-BTRC degradation)
rationale: Every member is NRF2 (NFE2L2) target-gene regulation or control of NRF2 itself, which separates it from the FOXO/UPR, ROS-detoxification and p53-metabolic neighbours.

head: Myeloid progenitor commitment to granulocytes
name: Myeloid progenitor commitment to granulocytes (transcriptional control, promyelocytes, monocyte-macrophage suppression)
rationale: Members describe progenitor proliferation, transcriptional granulopoiesis and repression of monocyte/macrophage fate, unlike the erythroid-megakaryocyte, monocyte and G-CSF/eosinophil neighbours.

head: Respiratory system development
name: Respiratory system development (lung branching and growth, pneumocyte differentiation, trachea and diaphragm)
rationale: Members build the lung, trachea and diaphragm; pneumocytes, trachea and diaphragm separate it from the surfactant and generic salivary-branching neighbours.

head: Gluconeogenic amino acid and choline-carnitine metabolism
name: Gluconeogenic amino acid and choline-carnitine metabolism (alanine, threonine, oxaloacetate)
rationale: Two unrelated strands (alanine/threonine feeding gluconeogenesis via oxaloacetate, and choline/carnitine metabolism) with no honest single idea; the pairing distinguishes it from the acyl-CoA, broad amino acid, TCA and biotin/carnitine-transport neighbours.

head: FGF receptor signaling
name: FGF receptor signaling (isoform-specific ligand binding, FRS/PLC/PI3K cascades, oncogenic mutants)
rationale: Nearly all members are FGFR1-4 ligand binding, downstream adaptor cascades or activating FGFR mutations, separating it from the broad RTK/RAS, ALK/PDGFR and drug-resistance neighbours.

head: Inherited glycogen synthesis defects
name: Inherited glycogen synthesis defects (glycogen synthase, glycogenin, branching enzyme)
rationale: All four are glycogen storage diseases of the synthesis enzymes, unlike neighbours centred on glycogen breakdown, glucose-6-phosphatase and glucokinase.

head: Endosomal TLR7/8/9 signaling regulation
name: Endosomal TLR7/8/9 signaling regulation (SLC15A4-TASL-IRF5 axis, self-ligand sensing)
rationale: Members regulate endosomal nucleic-acid TLRs, including IRF5 activation and defective TLR7 control by self ligands, rather than the cytosolic sensor or type I IFN output emphasised by neighbours.

head: Glutathione degradation and gamma-glutamyl cycle
name: Glutathione degradation and gamma-glutamyl cycle (GGT1/OPLAH/ACY1 defects, glutathione and cystine transport)
rationale: Members cover breakdown and transport of glutathione and its inborn errors, distinct from the glutathione synthesis and cystinuria/SLC transport neighbours.

head: Craniofacial development
name: Craniofacial development (olfactory system, trigeminal/facial nerves, lacrimal and salivary glands)
rationale: Members build nose, olfactory nerve and GnRH-neuron route, cranial nerves, taste papillae and head glands; olfactory and gland parts separate it from the ear and hindbrain neighbours.

head: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynapse assembly
name: Excitatory and inhibitory postsynapse assembly (neurexin-neuroligin, receptor clustering, glutamatergic transmission)
rationale: Members assemble glutamatergic and GABAergic postsynaptic sites and tune their potentials; glutamatergic transmission and inhibitory synapse parts separate it from the adhesion-focused neighbours.

head: Embryonic eye development
name: Embryonic eye development (optic cup and retina, retinal neuron differentiation, optic nerve)
rationale: Members form the optic cup, retinal layers and neurons, iris, eyelid and optic nerve, unlike neighbours on lens/cornea, retinal vasculature and phototransduction.

head: ER tubular network shaping
name: ER tubular network shaping (membrane bending, ER fusion, contact-site lipid transfer)
rationale: Members shape, fuse and position the ER tubular network and move lipids at its contacts, unlike the mitochondrial-contact and phosphoinositide neighbours.

head: Mitotic spindle assembly
name: Mitotic spindle assembly (centrosome separation, PLK1, NEK6/7/9 kinases)
rationale: Members drive centrosome separation and spindle formation via PLK1 and NEK kinases, unlike neighbours on the spindle checkpoint, midzone and Aurora A.

head: Eicosanoid synthesis and signaling
name: Eicosanoid synthesis and signaling (cyclooxygenase prostanoids, P450 HETEs and EETs, prostanoid receptors)
rationale: Members make arachidonate-derived eicosanoids by cyclooxygenase and P450 and act through prostanoid receptors, unlike the lipoxygenase, resolvin and leukotriene neighbours.

head: Collagen degradation
name: Collagen degradation (matrix metalloproteinase activation)
rationale: All three members concern collagen breakdown by activated MMPs, unlike the ECM-structure and fibrinolysis neighbours.

head: Neuropeptide GPCR signaling
name: Neuropeptide GPCR signaling (orexin wakefulness, opioid receptors, dense-core vesicle release)
rationale: Members are neuropeptide release and G-protein signaling including orexin-driven wakefulness, unlike neighbours on drug reward, sleep stages and stress behaviour.

head: Recombination-based telomere maintenance
name: Recombination-based telomere maintenance (break-induced replication, D-loop and t-circle control, telomere capping)
rationale: Members maintain and protect telomeres by recombination and break-induced replication, unlike neighbours on general DNA repair, telomere packaging and C-strand synthesis.

head: Interferon-stimulated host control of viral replication
name: Interferon-stimulated host control of viral replication (ISG15 conjugation, viral entry and release)
rationale: Members are ISG15 and other interferon-stimulated effects on viral entry, replication and release, unlike the OAS/PKR/IFN-signaling and generic viral life-cycle neighbours.

head: GPCR control of growth hormone release
name: GPCR control of growth hormone release (glucagon-family receptors, somatostatin receptors, adenylate cyclase)
rationale: Glucagon-family (GHRH) and somatostatin receptors steer cAMP and growth hormone secretion, unlike the GH-receptor, glucagon-metabolic and insulin-secretion neighbours.

head: Polyunsaturated fatty acid oxygenation
name: Polyunsaturated fatty acid oxygenation (lipoxygenase products, P450 HETEs and EETs, ichthyosis defects)
rationale: Members oxygenate arachidonate and linoleate by lipoxygenases and P450s, including skin-barrier ichthyosis genes, unlike the leukotriene-receptor, resolvin and cyclooxygenase neighbours.

head: Cochlear hair cell mechanotransduction
name: Cochlear hair cell mechanotransduction (stereocilia organization, inner hair cell sound processing)
rationale: All members concern sound detection by cochlear hair-cell stereocilia, unlike the vestibular, ear-morphogenesis and photoreceptor neighbours.

head: Immunoregulatory cytokine signaling
name: Immunoregulatory cytokine signaling (IL-12/23 and IL-10, IL-15 and IL-21, NK cell development)
rationale: Members are cytokines that steer lymphocyte and NK responses; IL-10/12/23 separate it from the interferon and IL-2/7 neighbours and IL-15/21 with NK development from the IL-27/35 neighbour.

head: Promotion of structural synaptic plasticity
name: Promotion of structural synaptic plasticity (dendritic spine morphogenesis, synapse maturation, local translation)
rationale: Members promote spine growth, synapse maturation and synaptic translation, unlike the CREB/memory, postsynaptic-actin and LTP/LTD neighbours.

head: Potentiation of synaptic transmission
name: Potentiation of synaptic transmission (glutamatergic and GABAergic, NCAM1 interactions, sensorimotor gating)
rationale: Members enhance glutamatergic and GABAergic transmission with prepulse inhibition and nonassociative learning, unlike the exploratory-behaviour, synapse-assembly and AMPA-receptor neighbours.

head: Protein glycan biosynthesis
name: Protein glycan biosynthesis (N- and O-glycans, glycosaminoglycan chains, fucosylated blood-group antigens)
rationale: Members build glycans on proteins and proteoglycans and their inherited defects, unlike the nucleotide-sugar transport and glycosphingolipid neighbours.
